fun_facts: Zay Flowers grew up in Fort Lauderdale, Florida, as the 11th of 14 children.
Across four seasons at Boston College, Zay Flowers had 200 catches, 3,056 receiving yards, and 29 touchdowns.
In 2022, Zay Flowers set Boston College’s single-season record with 78 catches; he also had 1,077 yards and 12 touchdowns that season.
Zay Flowers set Ravens rookie receiving records with 77 catches for 858 yards.
Zay Flowers became the first Ravens player to record a 1,000-yard receiving season within the first two years of his career.

excerpts:
* [Print](https://www.espn.com/espn/print?id=33860761)

Boston College star wide receiver [Zay Flowers](https://www.espn.com/college-football/player/_/id/4429615/zay-flowers) grew up in Fort Lauderdale, Florida, as the 11th of 14 children. His mother died in 2005, leaving his father, Willie, to drive a truck for a medical device company to provide for the family.

Flowers received a football scholarship to Boston College in 2019 and earned All-ACC honors as a wide receiver with a breakout 2020 season. He enters 2022 as one of the sport's best receivers and a strong NFL draft prospect.

"We all make mistakes," Jackson said. "It's his first season. It's my first time in this situation. It's his first time in this situation. We're going to bounce back. Nobody played the game perfect."

Flowers, who was the No. 22 pick of the 2023 draft, had the best rookie season for a wide receiver in team history. He set Ravens rookie records with 77 receptions for 858 yards.

In the AFC Championship Game, Flowers was the only impactful wide receiver for Baltimore. He caught five passes for 115 yards and scored on a 30-yard touchdown reception in the first quarter.
